correctness.rationale: Each word has q doubly occurring symbols; nesting obstructs equality and nonnesting admits a canonical split. Two interlaced pairs force equal first-occurrence colors; disjoint pairs impose no restriction. Components equal primitive Dyck excursions under the FIFO closing order, yielding 2^(r-1) witnesses. Catalan powers and singularity analysis prove the exact distribution and moments. Exhaustive direct checks of 116017 words through q=5 and 64 coefficient identities through q=32 agree. The infinite proof is combinatorial, not inferred from finite tests.

residual_risks: An unindexed theorem on interval-overlap graph components, Catalan returns or multiset shuffle witnesses might explicitly imply the refined distribution.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of ambiguity in unshuffling a linearly ordered word with exactly two copies per letter. It distinguishes uniquely decomposable words, gives all possible witness multiplicities and exact frequencies at every q, and exhibits bounded typical behavior versus linear first and exponential second moments. The quantitative certificate-complexity phenomenon is not obtained merely by reporting the established Catalan existence count.
